description.text: Program Description 1. Program Overview Editor Notes: As a graduate engineer, you will be able to deal with anything from power engineering to microelectronics, radar installations to the design of digital systems. Electrical and Electronic engineering graduates are qualified for professional practice or graduate work in several areas of specialization. In addition to the fundamentals of science and mathematics, the program provides a solid background in circuits, analog, and digital electronics, microprocessors, and electromagnetics. The senior-level classes offered for electrical/electronic engineers include control systems, communication systems, digital signal processing, electro-optics, and digital system design. The program is accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology. 2. Main Courses Editor Notes: The core courses which will be instructed in the 4 years are listed below. Spread Spectrum Communication Engineering Electromagnetic Field Matlab Applications Engineering Electromagnetic Field Microwave Technique and Antenna Signals and Systems Random Signal Analysis Digital Signal Processing Areospace Power Supply System Positioning and Navigation System 3. Future Career Fields After Graduation? Editor Notes: The fields listed below are most graduates choose to do after graduation. Broadcast engineer Control and instrumentation engineer Design engineer Electrical engineer Electronics engineer IT consultant Network engineer Nuclear engineer Systems analyst Military Service and other related technology-intensive fields 4. Accreditation: Accredited By The Ministry Of Education, China. NUAA's Degree Is Accepted Worldwide Editor Notes: Students can find their desirable job in the over 2000 on-campus recruitment fairs. NUAA's International Link: NUAA's degree allows you to take your project in China, your home country or a third country. NUAA has partnered with top universities in the USA, Australia, and the EU where some students take their third or fourth year of study. Career Prospects: NUAA has developed strong cooperation with several domestic and international enterprises. Collaboration between academia and industry is increasingly a critical component of efficient national and even global innovation systems. Every year over 2000 companies come to NUAA for on-campus recruitment fairs. 5. Introduction of Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics Editor Notes: World's top 150 Engineering Universities (U.S News Ranking 2018). Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics(NUAA) , established in 1952, enjoys a well-balanced development of multiple disciplines in natural sciences, humanities, social sciences, management, etc. with the characteristics of aeronautics, astronautics and civil aviation. NUAA is among the first batch of national key universities entitled to award doctoral degree, master's degree and bachelor's degree. It is one of the 52 universities with graduate school in China, and it has also been listed in the "National Project 211" as one of the 100 key universities for the 21st century. Presently, NUAA has established international cooperation and exchange with more than 60 universities and institutions all over the world. Learn More>> 6. Colourful Life Editor Notes: More colourful activities are waiting for you to explore. International Cultural Festival Mini-Graduation Ceremony

fields.description: Program Description Teaching Objective The curriculum system is established with the combination of arts, fashion and engineering through the multi-interdisciplinary approach to architecture, design and fine arts. By learning the fundamental theories and design methods of environmental design, students are expected to balance the relations between aesthetics and technology, space and structure, nature and humanities in their design works and develop the ability of creative thinking and design performance. The design studio system of Western interior design schools is introduced to this programme to encourage the students to gain design knowledge and independent design experience through project practice, furthermore, to motivate initiative of design and improve the problem-solving ability in real projects. Graduates shall have strong art design skills and work as designers or management talents in interior or outdoor environmental design sectors. Have a solid professional theoretical foundation, essentials of humanities, arts and social sciences as well as the ability of oral and written presentation. Systematically master the broad knowledge of technical theories in this discipline including architecture, design studies, shape and structure of space, architectural decoration materials, engineering graphics, etc. Have the essential ability of literature search, theoretical study, on-the-spot investigation, planning and design. Have a good command of basic skills such as engineering drawing, rendering expression and graphic design. Have a strong self-study ability and innovation consciousness. Have a global vision and fashion assessment capability and understand the development trends at the frontiers of the discipline. Main Courses Atelier Design, Catwalk Design, Window Display Design, Flagship Store Design, Fashion Exhibition Design, Residential Interior Design Studio, Restaurant&Cafe Design Studio, Industry Space Innovation Design Studio, Furniture Design Studio, Architecture Design, Landscape Design Studio, Environmental Facilities Design Studio, Public Art&Sculpture, Environmental Graphic Design Studio, Art History, Architectural History&Contemporary Architectural Trends, Landscape Design History, Professional&Key Skills, Computer Aided Interior Design Skills, Architecture Sketch, Architectural Decoration Materials&Processes, Lighting Design, Project Budget&Management, Environmental Psychology, Visual Culture, etc. Career Development Graduates may work as designers in design institutes, architectural construction companies and exhibition companies, or engage in project planning in design consulting and planning companies, project management in real estate companies or take the career path as art management brokers, etc. * The above is for reference only. The final course curriculum is subject to the arrangement of SCF. click here for more information about Environment Design: Fashion Interior Design

fields.description: Program Description Teaching Objective Through the courses, students are expected to learn basic theories, fundamental professional knowledge and practical skills of fashion design as well as understand the conception of design and learn the design methods. The programme emphasizes on the firm combination of theory and practice, merging the courses with international design trends to help students have a good command of the correct way of fashion design. Moreover, it focuses on training the conceptualization of design and innovation thinking to enable graduates to become high-ranking professionals in fashion design with a global vision, strong design consciousness and market competitiveness. The students will learn the basic theories of design and the basic skills of creative fashion design, understand the operation of the international fashion industry, and be familiar with the new trend of the internationa l creative fashion design. The students will have a solid knowledge of fashion history, and master the skills of fashion design, pattern and technology. The students will be able to analyze the fashion market with innovative thinking, have a good sense of aesthetics and the comprehensive ability for fashion and accessory design; The students will be able to communicate in English in any social and professional environment. Main Courses Computer Aided Fashion Design, Structure and Fomi in Design, Fashion Structure and Technics, Design Software for Fashion, Portfolio, Architects the Body, Fashion Illustration, Creative Pattern Manipulation, Fashion Pattern Design, History of Costume, Creative Menswear Interpretation, Fashion Accessory Design, Fashion Branding, From Trend to Design Idea, Knitwear Design, Fashion Design of Fashion Brand, Resolve-Prototype Collection,etc. Career Development Graduates may work for Chinese and international fashion brands, luxury brands,design studios, fashion publishing and media, or engage in fashion design, fabric design, garment pattern design, fashion editing, brand management and sales. Graduates are also encouraged to create personal fashion brands, establish design studios, or further study for a master's degree.

ID photo Recent bareheaded(within six months), full-face, white-color background, two-inch certificate photo,instead of landscape photos or photos of daily life; in JPG format, less than 100K. * 2. English language proficiency * 3. High school academic transcripts Copies of the original certificate with the high school stamp and/or the signature of the principal. If the originals are not in Chinese or English, it must be translated and notarized. Students who are currently in the final year can submit a pending certificate along with transcripts of all grades you completed. You are required to submit the official certificate and final transcripts once you receive them. * 4. Statement of financial support To be filled out and signed by the applicant and the financial guarantor. The signing date should be on or after November 1, 2025. You can download a template or sample from here . 5. Mandatory for application of art design related programs 1. Applicants for the Chinese-taught program majored in Fashion & Apparel Design, Product Design, Environmental Design, Visual Communication Design, Digital Media Art, or Art & Technology, you are required to submit the original latest art works: at least two hand-painted pencil sketch, two hand-painted color painting, and three design rendering relating to the applied program. 2. For applications to the two English-taught programs, a video-formatted personal art portfolio must be submitted. The video should feature explanations in English, covering the applicant's design concepts, demonstrating their understanding of professional knowledge, mastery of skills, and creativity, with a duration of approximately 3 minutes. 3. If notified by Donghua University via email to participate in an art examination or related interview (latest by June), applicants should respond and participate as scheduled. The results will serve as an important reference for the university's decision. * 6. Certificate of no criminal conviction Issued by the local public security authority or relevant government department in the applicant's location. The issue date should be on or after November 1, 2025. * 7. Personal Resume (1) Written in the teaching language of the applied DHU program. (2) Include basic personal information, self-assessment, hobbies and interests, skills and strengths, contact details, and educational background (with timelines precise to the month). (3) List participation in relevant activities or competitions, internships or practical experiences, honors or awards received, and certificates of competency, etc. Relevant certificates and supporting documents can be merged into one PDF file and uploaded under "Other Supplementary Documents" session. * 8. Passport (and visa) page A clear copy of your valid passport with your name, photo, date of birth, place of birth, date of issue and date of expiry. The passport should have at least 6-month validity. All visa pages are required if you have been to or if you are currently in China. * 9. Personal statement (1) Written in the teaching language of the applied DHU program, approximately 1000 words. (2) Describe family background and educational experience, reasons for choosing the major and motivation for application, significant experiences and gains related to the applied major, academic and career prospects and plans, etc., to showcase personal thoughts and characteristics, abilities, and strengths. (3) Must include the applicant's full name, the applied major, personal email address, and the date of writing at the end of the statement. * 10. High school graduation certificate Copies of the original certificate with the high school stamp and/or the signature of the principal. If the original is not in Chinese or English, it must be translated and notarized. Students who are currently in the final year can submit a pending certificate along with transcripts of all grades you completed. You are required to submit the official certificate and final transcripts once you receive them. * 11. CSCA Test Transcript(s) -You need to take the official CSCA test organized by the Chinese government and submit the corresponding subject result transcript(s) when applying. Learn more about the CSCA test >> -The test covers Chinese (Humanities and STEM Chinese), Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry. Mathematics is required for all programs, while other subjects depend on the university’s specific requirements. -We are updating detailed information for each university, including the required subjects you have to take for each program and their score requirements. Once the updates are ready, you can check the attachment and information here for this university for the latest information. If no attachment is available yet, it usually means the university has not announced further details. You can download a template or sample from here . Tips: For applicants who are in China: If you are an employee, you still need to provide employment separation certificate and your current residence permit. If you are a student, you need to provide transfer certificate, leaving certificate, certificate of attendance rate issued by previous school and your current residence permit.

description.text: Program Description Teaching Objective Through the courses, students are expected to learn basic theories, fundamental professional knowledge and practical skills of fashion design as well as understand the conception of design and learn the design methods. The programme emphasizes on the firm combination of theory and practice, merging the courses with international design trends to help students have a good command of the correct way of fashion design. Moreover, it focuses on training the conceptualization of design and innovation thinking to enable graduates to become high-ranking professionals in fashion design with a global vision, strong design consciousness and market competitiveness. The students will learn the basic theories of design and the basic skills of creative fashion design, understand the operation of the international fashion industry, and be familiar with the new trend of the internationa l creative fashion design. The students will have a solid knowledge of fashion history, and master the skills of fashion design, pattern and technology. The students will be able to analyze the fashion market with innovative thinking, have a good sense of aesthetics and the comprehensive ability for fashion and accessory design; The students will be able to communicate in English in any social and professional environment. Main Courses Computer Aided Fashion Design, Structure and Fomi in Design, Fashion Structure and Technics, Design Software for Fashion, Portfolio, Architects the Body, Fashion Illustration, Creative Pattern Manipulation, Fashion Pattern Design, History of Costume, Creative Menswear Interpretation, Fashion Accessory Design, Fashion Branding, From Trend to Design Idea, Knitwear Design, Fashion Design of Fashion Brand, Resolve-Prototype Collection,etc. Career Development Graduates may work for Chinese and international fashion brands, luxury brands,design studios, fashion publishing and media, or engage in fashion design, fabric design, garment pattern design, fashion editing, brand management and sales. Graduates are also encouraged to create personal fashion brands, establish design studios, or further study for a master's degree.

fields.requirements: Entry Requirements Applicants should be non-Chinese citizens with a valid private ordinary passport. Note: Whether an applicant who holds foreign nationality also possesses the nationality of the People’s Republic of China shall be determined by the nationality appraisal issued by the Exit and Entry Administration of the Chinese public-security authorities. If an applicant is determined to hold Chinese nationality or is otherwise ineligible at any point during the application, admission, or enrollment process, their application, offer of admission, or student status will be revoked. Applicants should be in good physical and mental health, and meet the medical examination requirements of both the country and the university. Applicants should not have criminal record and maintain a friendly attitude towards China. Furthermore, applicants must be well-behaved and willing to comply with Chinese laws and regulations, as well as the rules of SJTU. Doctoral degree program applicants should have a Master’s degree or an equivalent degree (or above) accepted in China. For programs taught in English All international applicants for admission to any SJTU program must provide evidence that their English language proficiency meets the minimum requirements for admission. Being born in a native English-speaking country is not a proof of your English proficiency. You will be deemed to have satisfied the English language requirements if you can provide evidence that you meet one or more of the following criteria: i)English Language Tests ii) Prior study in the medium of English a) English Language Tests SJTU recognizes a number of English Language tests and English Preparation Courses which can be undertaken to meet the University’s English language requirements. These are set out in the following table, together with the minimum results required. The test/score must be valid till the year of application. For example, the TOEFL must have been undertaken no more than two years prior to the commencement of the program at SJTU, i.e., the test must be dated on or after 1 January (two years prior) for Fall Semester intake. b) Priorstudy in the medium of English If you have successfully completed an assessable Senior Secondary qualification or a post-secondary/tertiary study at an accredited university from an English-speaking country* you do not have to prove proficiency in English provided the qualification was: i) Taught and examined in English ii) Completed no more than two years prior to the commencement of the program at SJTU. iii) The statement or certificate must be on official headed paper, and must be the original document. * English-speaking countries recognized by SJTU international graduate programs include: American Samoa, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Botswana, Canada, Fiji, Gibraltar, Ghana, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Papua New Guinea, Singapore, Solomon Islands, South Africa, The Gambia, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, United Kingdom (including Northern Ireland), United States of America, Zambia, Zimbabwe.

fields.description: Program Description To obtain a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) Degree in Mechanical Engineering (ME) or Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) from the Joint Institute, students must fulfill the following requirements. Complete specific coursework sequence, which differs for students starting their Doctoral program with a Bachelor’s Degree or with a Master’s Degree . Preparation, propose, and defend a Doctoral Thesis . While the typical duration of the doctoral program is of five years for students starting their Doctoral program with a Bachelor’s degree and of three to four years for students starting their Doctoral program with a Master’s degree, students are eligible to receive a doctoral degree when the above requirements are fulfilled. Requirements for ME and ECE degrees are identical; the term “major” refers to the ME and ECE programs. 1. Coursework (Students entering with Bachelor’s degree only) To complete their coursework requirement, Doctoral students entering the doctoral program with a Bachelor’s degree must take a number of courses, while maintaining a minimum GPA. Specifically, students must take the following course. At least thirty nine approved credit hours of engineering, math, and science at the 4xx level or higher, A total of three credit hours of technical communication, Vg 500 Technical Communication, and A total of three credit hours of politics. The JI Grade Point Average for these courses must be at least 3.3. The thirty-nine approved credit hours of engineering, math, and science are subjected to the following restrictions. At least six credit hours of mathematics must be taken at the 5xx level or higher. At least fifteen credit hours within the student’s major must be selected at the 5xx level or higher. A maximum of twelve credit hours may be selected from classes offered outside of the JI. These credit hours must be approved by the faculty adviser and the graduate committee . The Petition to Take a Non-JI Course form can be downloaded from the Graduate Student Forms . The total number of 4xx level courses cannot exceed nine credit hours. Students must take at least six credit hours outside their discipline group to ensure the breadth of their study program. The combined total of 4xx level credit hours and credit hours taken outside of the JI cannot exceed fifteen. If the Graduate Committee approves a non-JI math class to satisfy the math requirement, those non-JI math credits do not count toward this total of fifteen credit hours. 2. Coursework (Students entering with Master’s degree) To complete their coursework requirement, Doctoral students entering the doctoral program with a Master’s degree must take a number of courses, while maintaining a minimum GPA. Specifically, students must take the following course. At least eighteen approved credit hours of engineering, math, and science at the 4xx level or higher, and A total of three credit hours of technical communication, Vg 500 Technical Communication. The JI Grade Point Average for these courses must be at least 3.3. The eighteen approved credit hours of engineering, math, and science are subjected to the following restrictions. At least nine credit hours within the student’s major must be selected at the 5xx level or higher. A maximum of six credit hours may be selected from classes offered outside of the JI. These credit hours must be approved by the faculty adviser and the graduate committee . The Petition to Take a Non-JI Course form can be downloaded from the Graduate Student Forms . Students must take at least three credit hours outside their disciple group to ensure the breadth of their study program. If the Graduate Committee approves a non-JI math class to satisfy the math requirement, those non-JI math credits do not count toward this total of six credit hours. 3. Qualifying Grade Point Average Doctoral students must write and defend of a formal doctoral thesis. For each semester they are involved in graduate research, ME or ECE students must register for doctoral thesis research, Vm 695 or Ve 695 Doctoral Thesis, respectively. This course will provide feedback on their progress toward the completion of their doctoral thesis. For the first step of their doctoral program, students must become qualified doctoral students. This status is achieved through coursework only. For students entering with a Bachelor’s degree, the GPA for their first five courses at the 5xx level or above must be at least 3.5 . For students entering with a Master’s degree, the GPA for their first three courses at the 5xx level or above must be at least 3.5. These classes must be completed within the first two years of the student’s doctoral program of studies. Upon completion of these five courses, students submit a Petition to become a qualified doctoral student to the graduate office. If a student fails to achieve the qualifying GPA, the graduate committee will review their record. The graduate committee will take either of the following two actions: (1) dismiss the student from the Doctoral program, or, (2) specify additional coursework and target grades needed to continue in the Doctoral program. 4. The Candidacy Exam For the second step of their doctoral program, students must pass the candidacy exam. Students entering with a Bachelor’s degree should schedule their candidacy exam after completing a minimum of thirty approved credits hours and within the third year of their program of studies. Students entering with a Master’s degree should schedule their candidacy exam after completing a minimum of twelve approved credits hours and within the second year of their program of studies. The candidacy exam consists of a ninety-minute, oral examination administered by three distinct faculty members. For their candidacy exam, students select three courses, at least one of which is in their discipline area and at least two of which are within their major. Each of the three courses will be the basis for a thirty-minute portion of the oral examination. After completion of the examination, each candidate receives three marks, one from each of the three faculty members who administered the exam. To pass the candidacy exam, a minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. The outcome of the examination is recorded in the Candidacy Exam Form . Two examination sessions are scheduled during each academic year, one during the fall and one during the summer semester. If a student fails the candidacy exam, he/she must retake the exam at the next available session. If unsuccessful at the second try, the student will be dismissed from the doctoral program. Upon successful completion of the candidacy exam, the student becomes a doctoral student candidate. 4.1. The discipline areas Candidacy exam sessions will be scheduled twice during each academic year. Candidates will choose the three courses that form the basis of the candidacy examination from the list of gateway courses below. In Mechanical Engineering, the discipline areas and associated gateway courses are as follows. Design and Manufacturing: Vm551 Mechanisms Design, Vm583 Manufacturing Processes and Systems. Dynamics and Vibrations: Vm 543 : Analytical Dynamics, Vm 541 : Mechanical Vibrations. Fluid Mechanics and Thermal Sciences: Vm530 Advanced Heat Transfer, Vm523 Advanced Fluid Mechanics / Comp Fluid Dynamics. Solid Mechanics, Structures, and Materials: Vm 510 : Advanced Structural Analysis, Vm 511 : Foundation of Solid Mechanics. Mechatronics and Control: Vm564 Linear Systems, Vm552 Mechatronic Systems. In Electrical and Computer Engineering, the discipline areas and associated gateway courses are as follows. Computer Architecture and Engineering: Ve527 Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits. Electromagnetism, Optics, and Photonics: Ve 5xx abc, Ve 5xx, def. Circuits and Devices: Ve 5xx abc, Ve 5xx, def. Communications and Networking: Ve 5xx abc, Ve 5xx, def. Signal Processing: Ve501 Probability and Random Processes. 5. The Doctoral Dissertation The completion of the doctoral dissertation involves the following steps: (1) form the Doctoral Dissertation Committee, (2) call for one or more Doctoral Research Meetings, (3) develop a Dissertation Proposal, and (4) defend the Doctoral Dissertation. The time line for the doctoral thesis is presented in figs. 1 and 2. 5.1. The doctoral dissertation committee After successful completion of their candidacy exam and in consultation with their research adviser, students invite a minimum of five faculty members to serve on their Doctoral Dissertation Committee . This committee will guide, monitor, and assess the student’s progress thereafter. The membership of the dissertation committee is subjected to the following requirements. (1) The head of the dissertation committee is the student’s thesis adviser, (2) the second member of the committee is a member of JI’s faculty within the student’s major, (3) the third member is a member of JI’s faculty outside the student’s major, and (4) the fourth and fifth members must hold a doctoral degree. The membership of the dissertation committee must be approved by JI’s degree committee. The Doctoral dissertation committee membership form must be submitted to the Graduate Program Coordinator for approval by the degree committee. 5.2. The doctoral research meeting Doctoral candidates will call a research meeting with their dissertation committee. The purpose of this research meeting is to promote early planning of the doctoral thesis. The goals of the meeting are as follows: (1) give guidance concerning the proposed research plan in terms of scope, feasibility, and suitability for a doctoral thesis, (2) provide constructive feedback to the student, (3) assess the student’s familiarity with the literature in the field, and (4) delineate the expected technical contributions of the thesis. If the dissertation committee deems it necessary, follow-up research meetings will be recommended. The dissertation committee can, after two or more unsatisfactory research meetings, dismiss the doctoral candidate from the doctoral program if they believe he/she is not capable of completing an acceptable doctoral dissertation. The outcome of the doctoral research meeting is recorded in the Research Meeting Minutes Form . If follow up research meetings were held, this form documents the conclusions of all research meetings. 5.3. The doctoral dissertation proposal The candidate then writes his/her doctoral thesis proposal. This document provides the following information: (1) the proposed content of the research work, (2) a comprehensive literature review of the state-of-the-art in the field, (3) a description of the research tasks that have been completed, (4) a discussion of preliminary results, (5) the original contribution of the proposed research, and (6) the tasks that will be completed before the thesis defense. Next, the student presents his/her doctoral thesis proposal to the dissertation committee. This presentation must be open to the public. A minimum of one month should elapse between the research meeting and the thesis proposal. The environment is one of open discussion among the student, adviser, and dissertation committee members. The purpose is not to examine the student’s technical ability but to review of the doctoral research proposal. The dissertation committee must approve the dissertation proposal unanimously. If a unanimous vote cannot be reached, an additional thesis proposals must be scheduled after the student’s response to the concerns raised by all members of the dissertation committee. The outcome of the doctoral dissertation proposal is recorded in the Dissertation Proposal Minutes Form . Figure 1. The doctoral thesis proposal time line 5.4. The dissertation defense Once the dissertation is completed, the candidate sends draft copies to the members of the dissertation committee with at least two weeks for their review. The committee will suggest corrections and modifications of the dissertation. The head of the dissertation committee then decides whether the draft dissertation is ready for defense. If not, the student will modify the draft of the doctoral thesis in accordance with committee’s recommendations. Resubmission of the dissertation to the committee is then required for final approval. Upon approval of the draft doctoral dissertation by the head of the dissertation committee, the candidate is allowed to schedule his/her doctoral dissertation defense. A minimum of one year must elapse between the dissertation proposal and the dissertation defense. ​ Figure 2. The doctoral dissertation time line The candidate then schedules a public oral defense of his/her dissertation. The dissertation committee must approve the dissertation defense unanimously. If a unanimous vote cannot be reached, the student must respond to the concerns raised by all members of the committee and an additional public defense must be scheduled in consultation with the dissertation committee. The outcome of the doctoral dissertation defense is recorded in the Dissertation Defense Minutes Form . 6. Important dates SJTU accepts the final dissertation at four dates. They are March 15, June 30, September 30 and December 15. So accordingly the doctoral dissertation due time at the JI will be March 1, June 15, September 15 and December 1. Tuition The tuition of Ph.D. students working as teaching or research assistants is waived. In addition, Ph.D. students receive a monthly stipend of 2,500 RMB; after qualification as doctoral students, this stipend will be raised to 2,800 RMB. After passing the candidacy exam, student’s monthly stipend is raised to 3,500 RMB.

description.text: Program Description To obtain a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) Degree in Mechanical Engineering (ME) or Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) from the Joint Institute, students must fulfill the following requirements. Complete specific coursework sequence, which differs for students starting their Doctoral program with a Bachelor’s Degree or with a Master’s Degree . Preparation, propose, and defend a Doctoral Thesis . While the typical duration of the doctoral program is of five years for students starting their Doctoral program with a Bachelor’s degree and of three to four years for students starting their Doctoral program with a Master’s degree, students are eligible to receive a doctoral degree when the above requirements are fulfilled. Requirements for ME and ECE degrees are identical; the term “major” refers to the ME and ECE programs. 1. Coursework (Students entering with Bachelor’s degree only) To complete their coursework requirement, Doctoral students entering the doctoral program with a Bachelor’s degree must take a number of courses, while maintaining a minimum GPA. Specifically, students must take the following course. At least thirty nine approved credit hours of engineering, math, and science at the 4xx level or higher, A total of three credit hours of technical communication, Vg 500 Technical Communication, and A total of three credit hours of politics. The JI Grade Point Average for these courses must be at least 3.3. The thirty-nine approved credit hours of engineering, math, and science are subjected to the following restrictions. At least six credit hours of mathematics must be taken at the 5xx level or higher. At least fifteen credit hours within the student’s major must be selected at the 5xx level or higher. A maximum of twelve credit hours may be selected from classes offered outside of the JI. These credit hours must be approved by the faculty adviser and the graduate committee . The Petition to Take a Non-JI Course form can be downloaded from the Graduate Student Forms . The total number of 4xx level courses cannot exceed nine credit hours. Students must take at least six credit hours outside their discipline group to ensure the breadth of their study program. The combined total of 4xx level credit hours and credit hours taken outside of the JI cannot exceed fifteen. If the Graduate Committee approves a non-JI math class to satisfy the math requirement, those non-JI math credits do not count toward this total of fifteen credit hours. 2. Coursework (Students entering with Master’s degree) To complete their coursework requirement, Doctoral students entering the doctoral program with a Master’s degree must take a number of courses, while maintaining a minimum GPA. Specifically, students must take the following course. At least eighteen approved credit hours of engineering, math, and science at the 4xx level or higher, and A total of three credit hours of technical communication, Vg 500 Technical Communication. The JI Grade Point Average for these courses must be at least 3.3. The eighteen approved credit hours of engineering, math, and science are subjected to the following restrictions. At least nine credit hours within the student’s major must be selected at the 5xx level or higher. A maximum of six credit hours may be selected from classes offered outside of the JI. These credit hours must be approved by the faculty adviser and the graduate committee . The Petition to Take a Non-JI Course form can be downloaded from the Graduate Student Forms . Students must take at least three credit hours outside their disciple group to ensure the breadth of their study program. If the Graduate Committee approves a non-JI math class to satisfy the math requirement, those non-JI math credits do not count toward this total of six credit hours. 3. Qualifying Grade Point Average Doctoral students must write and defend of a formal doctoral thesis. For each semester they are involved in graduate research, ME or ECE students must register for doctoral thesis research, Vm 695 or Ve 695 Doctoral Thesis, respectively. This course will provide feedback on their progress toward the completion of their doctoral thesis. For the first step of their doctoral program, students must become qualified doctoral students. This status is achieved through coursework only. For students entering with a Bachelor’s degree, the GPA for their first five courses at the 5xx level or above must be at least 3.5 . For students entering with a Master’s degree, the GPA for their first three courses at the 5xx level or above must be at least 3.5. These classes must be completed within the first two years of the student’s doctoral program of studies. Upon completion of these five courses, students submit a Petition to become a qualified doctoral student to the graduate office. If a student fails to achieve the qualifying GPA, the graduate committee will review their record. The graduate committee will take either of the following two actions: (1) dismiss the student from the Doctoral program, or, (2) specify additional coursework and target grades needed to continue in the Doctoral program. 4. The Candidacy Exam For the second step of their doctoral program, students must pass the candidacy exam. Students entering with a Bachelor’s degree should schedule their candidacy exam after completing a minimum of thirty approved credits hours and within the third year of their program of studies. Students entering with a Master’s degree should schedule their candidacy exam after completing a minimum of twelve approved credits hours and within the second year of their program of studies. The candidacy exam consists of a ninety-minute, oral examination administered by three distinct faculty members. For their candidacy exam, students select three courses, at least one of which is in their discipline area and at least two of which are within their major. Each of the three courses will be the basis for a thirty-minute portion of the oral examination. After completion of the examination, each candidate receives three marks, one from each of the three faculty members who administered the exam. To pass the candidacy exam, a minimum GPA of 3.0 is required. The outcome of the examination is recorded in the Candidacy Exam Form . Two examination sessions are scheduled during each academic year, one during the fall and one during the summer semester. If a student fails the candidacy exam, he/she must retake the exam at the next available session. If unsuccessful at the second try, the student will be dismissed from the doctoral program. Upon successful completion of the candidacy exam, the student becomes a doctoral student candidate. 4.1. The discipline areas Candidacy exam sessions will be scheduled twice during each academic year. Candidates will choose the three courses that form the basis of the candidacy examination from the list of gateway courses below. In Mechanical Engineering, the discipline areas and associated gateway courses are as follows. Design and Manufacturing: Vm551 Mechanisms Design, Vm583 Manufacturing Processes and Systems. Dynamics and Vibrations: Vm 543 : Analytical Dynamics, Vm 541 : Mechanical Vibrations. Fluid Mechanics and Thermal Sciences: Vm530 Advanced Heat Transfer, Vm523 Advanced Fluid Mechanics / Comp Fluid Dynamics. Solid Mechanics, Structures, and Materials: Vm 510 : Advanced Structural Analysis, Vm 511 : Foundation of Solid Mechanics. Mechatronics and Control: Vm564 Linear Systems, Vm552 Mechatronic Systems. In Electrical and Computer Engineering, the discipline areas and associated gateway courses are as follows. Computer Architecture and Engineering: Ve527 Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits. Electromagnetism, Optics, and Photonics: Ve 5xx abc, Ve 5xx, def. Circuits and Devices: Ve 5xx abc, Ve 5xx, def. Communications and Networking: Ve 5xx abc, Ve 5xx, def. Signal Processing: Ve501 Probability and Random Processes. 5. The Doctoral Dissertation The completion of the doctoral dissertation involves the following steps: (1) form the Doctoral Dissertation Committee, (2) call for one or more Doctoral Research Meetings, (3) develop a Dissertation Proposal, and (4) defend the Doctoral Dissertation. The time line for the doctoral thesis is presented in figs. 1 and 2. 5.1. The doctoral dissertation committee After successful completion of their candidacy exam and in consultation with their research adviser, students invite a minimum of five faculty members to serve on their Doctoral Dissertation Committee . This committee will guide, monitor, and assess the student’s progress thereafter. The membership of the dissertation committee is subjected to the following requirements. (1) The head of the dissertation committee is the student’s thesis adviser, (2) the second member of the committee is a member of JI’s faculty within the student’s major, (3) the third member is a member of JI’s faculty outside the student’s major, and (4) the fourth and fifth members must hold a doctoral degree. The membership of the dissertation committee must be approved by JI’s degree committee. The Doctoral dissertation committee membership form must be submitted to the Graduate Program Coordinator for approval by the degree committee. 5.2. The doctoral research meeting Doctoral candidates will call a research meeting with their dissertation committee. The purpose of this research meeting is to promote early planning of the doctoral thesis. The goals of the meeting are as follows: (1) give guidance concerning the proposed research plan in terms of scope, feasibility, and suitability for a doctoral thesis, (2) provide constructive feedback to the student, (3) assess the student’s familiarity with the literature in the field, and (4) delineate the expected technical contributions of the thesis. If the dissertation committee deems it necessary, follow-up research meetings will be recommended. The dissertation committee can, after two or more unsatisfactory research meetings, dismiss the doctoral candidate from the doctoral program if they believe he/she is not capable of completing an acceptable doctoral dissertation. The outcome of the doctoral research meeting is recorded in the Research Meeting Minutes Form . If follow up research meetings were held, this form documents the conclusions of all research meetings. 5.3. The doctoral dissertation proposal The candidate then writes his/her doctoral thesis proposal. This document provides the following information: (1) the proposed content of the research work, (2) a comprehensive literature review of the state-of-the-art in the field, (3) a description of the research tasks that have been completed, (4) a discussion of preliminary results, (5) the original contribution of the proposed research, and (6) the tasks that will be completed before the thesis defense. Next, the student presents his/her doctoral thesis proposal to the dissertation committee. This presentation must be open to the public. A minimum of one month should elapse between the research meeting and the thesis proposal. The environment is one of open discussion among the student, adviser, and dissertation committee members. The purpose is not to examine the student’s technical ability but to review of the doctoral research proposal. The dissertation committee must approve the dissertation proposal unanimously. If a unanimous vote cannot be reached, an additional thesis proposals must be scheduled after the student’s response to the concerns raised by all members of the dissertation committee. The outcome of the doctoral dissertation proposal is recorded in the Dissertation Proposal Minutes Form . Figure 1. The doctoral thesis proposal time line 5.4. The dissertation defense Once the dissertation is completed, the candidate sends draft copies to the members of the dissertation committee with at least two weeks for their review. The committee will suggest corrections and modifications of the dissertation. The head of the dissertation committee then decides whether the draft dissertation is ready for defense. If not, the student will modify the draft of the doctoral thesis in accordance with committee’s recommendations. Resubmission of the dissertation to the committee is then required for final approval. Upon approval of the draft doctoral dissertation by the head of the dissertation committee, the candidate is allowed to schedule his/her doctoral dissertation defense. A minimum of one year must elapse between the dissertation proposal and the dissertation defense. ​ Figure 2. The doctoral dissertation time line The candidate then schedules a public oral defense of his/her dissertation. The dissertation committee must approve the dissertation defense unanimously. If a unanimous vote cannot be reached, the student must respond to the concerns raised by all members of the committee and an additional public defense must be scheduled in consultation with the dissertation committee. The outcome of the doctoral dissertation defense is recorded in the Dissertation Defense Minutes Form . 6. Important dates SJTU accepts the final dissertation at four dates. They are March 15, June 30, September 30 and December 15. So accordingly the doctoral dissertation due time at the JI will be March 1, June 15, September 15 and December 1. Tuition The tuition of Ph.D. students working as teaching or research assistants is waived. In addition, Ph.D. students receive a monthly stipend of 2,500 RMB; after qualification as doctoral students, this stipend will be raised to 2,800 RMB. After passing the candidacy exam, student’s monthly stipend is raised to 3,500 RMB.

fields.requirements: Entry Requirements 1. Non-Chinese citizens, physically and mentally healthy, able to meet the normal study and life at school. 2. High school graduate with high school diploma or above. 3. Friendly towards China, law-abiding, and no criminal record. Others If both or one of the parents is a Chinese citizen and resides in a foreign country, and the applicant who wants to come to China as a foreign student for undergraduate study has foreign nationality by birth, then the applicant must have a record of actual residence in a foreign country for more than 2 years within the last 4 years (as of April 30, 2025). (Nine (9) months of actual residence in a foreign country can be counted as one year, subject to the entry and exit seal stamps). If a Chinese citizen after emigrating abroad applies to come to China as a foreign student for undergraduate study, then they shall hold a valid foreign passport or certificate of nationality for more than 4 years, and a record of actual residence in a foreign country for more than 2 years within the last 4 years (as of April 30, 2025). (Nine (9) months of actual residence in a foreign country can be counted as one year, subject to the entry and exit seal stamps).

fields.description: Program Description 1) Training requirements: 1. Adapted to all the four Chinese language abilities used in Chinese teaching environment, including listening, speaking, reading and writing skills 2. Master some basic professional knowledge 3. Gradually adapt to the teaching methods and learning methods of the university 4. Have the ability to learn and think independently. 2) Program categories Chinese Class (long term): The long-term class (more than half a year) enrolls students twice a year, starting in March and September respectively, with different levels: primary, intermediate and advanced courses. The core courses include: reading and writing, listening and speaking, reading, intensive reading, scientific Chinese, and Chinese culture, etc. According to the applicants’ application and class placement interview results, several small classes will be organized for teaching. Each class will have listening, speaking, reading and writing courses to comprehensively develop students' four skills. Classes will run from Monday to Friday. Every week 22-30 class hours will be arranged. In addition, there will be special tutoringcourses for HSK. ※ During the epidemic, online Chinese language classes will be provided. After the outbreak, the registration fee will be waived for online students who continue to study offline. 3) Completion and further education Upon completion: Students who pass the required courses and obtain the required credits will be awarded the Certificate of Completion for Chinese Language Training issued by the Institute of International Education. Further education: Students who have completed all the teaching procedures prescribed in the training program and passed the undergraduate qualification examination can directly enter the undergraduate program of our university. Those who do not meet the eligibility criteria for completion or fail to pass the qualification examination for admission to the undergraduate program may continue to study in the language program until they pass.

fields.requirements: Entry Requirements 1. Registration Requirements 1.1 Eligibility Criteria To apply to Jinan University, international students must meet the following requirements: Educational Qualification: Must possess a high school diploma or an equivalent educational level. Age: Must be over 18 years and not exceeding 25 years old. Conduct: Must have good conduct and a clean criminal record. Health: Must be physically and mentally healthy. 1.2 Additional Requirements In addition to the above general requirements, students who meet the following conditions are eligible to apply: - Overseas Chinese Students: Students who holds foreign nationality by birth, with at least one parent who is a Chinese citizen residing abroad. - Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan Residents: Students who are residents of Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan, and have obtained foreign nationality through immigration. To qualify as international students studying in China, these applicants must also fulfill the following: Passport Validity: Hold a valid foreign passport or nationality certificate for at least 4 years. Residency Requirement: Have a record of actual residence in foreign countries for more than 2 years within the past 4 years (from May 1, 2021, to April 30, 2025). Note: Time spent in foreign countries for more than 9 months in a year can be counted as one year.Entry and exit signatures will be used to verify residency. 1.3 Language Proficiency Requirements Applicants must meet the following language proficiency requirements based on the language of instruction for their chosen major: For International School (English-Taught Majors): Non-native English speakers must demonstrate English proficiency through one of the following: - IELTS: Minimum overall score of 5.5, with no section below 5.0 - TOEFL (IBT): Minimum score of 80 - SAT: Minimum total score of 1030
fields.materials: Application Materials " * " means necessary documents that you must provide in your application. If you want to book our translation service , please pay and book it at least 2 weeks before the application deadline for submission of all documents; If you want to book our guardian service , you need to pay and book it 2 months before the application deadline, just in case your application fails because of failed to submit application documents on time. * 1. Certificate of No Criminal Record -Please note that this document is valid for only 3 months. For instance, if you submit your -application in April, your non-criminal record must have been issued no earlier than January. -Obtain a police clearance certificate from the local police station where you currently reside, confirming no criminal record in the past 6 months at the time of application. -You need to translated it into CHINESE if it is not in Chinese; Then you need to get it notarized by local notary office and then get it certified by local Chinese embassy; If your country has joined the HAGUE convention then just do the Chinese translation and Apostille; Then you may need to mail original copy of non-criminal record and translation & certified(or Apostille) documents to the university in China. -If you are currently in China, the certificate must be issued by the local Chinese police. * 2. Recommendation Letter One letter of recommendation, which can be from: Jinan University’s overseas student recruitment agencies Local overseas Chinese organizations Well-known figures in the overseas Chinese community The graduating high school * 3. Personal Statement A self-introduction that includes past learning experiences and study plans while in China. * 4. Physical Examination Report The students who apply for medical majors should provide a physical examination report from the past six months. The Physical Examination Form template is provided in the attachment of this guide.. You can download a template or sample from here . 5. As per the Notice of the Ministry of Education on Standardizing the Acceptance of International Students in Our Higher Education Institutions (Doc. [2020] No. 12), the following documents are required For applicants who were originally residents of the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan and later acquired foreign nationality: Certificate of cancellation of Chinese nationality or registered residence. Certificate of foreign nationality acquisition. Entry and exit records for the past four years (up to April 30, 2025). For applicants who obtained foreign nationality at birth (if either or both parents are Chinese citizens): Proof of foreign nationality obtained at birth. Permanent residence certificate of the applicant’s Chinese parents in a foreign country before birth. Entry and exit records for the past four years (up to April 30, 2025). * 6. English Proficiency Certificates * 7. Passport A copy of the applicant’s passport. If currently in China, the most recent valid Chinese visa page and entry/exit record seals must also be provided. * 8. Passport photo A recent passport-sized photo of the applicant * 9. Transcripts for each academic year of high school issued by the graduating high school. Transcript issued by a foreign authority must be notarized or authenticated by a Chinese embassy or consulate abroad. If the country where the document is issued is a contracting state of the Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalization for Foreign Public Documents, an Apostille is sufficient. No consular authentication is required. Internationally standardized exam transcripts (if available), such as SAT/ACT/A-Level/ AP/IB, etc. * 10. A graduation certificate or proof of high school education or higher. Graduation Certificate issued by a foreign authority must be notarized or authenticated by a Chinese embassy or consulate abroad. If the country where the document is issued is a contracting state of the Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalization for Foreign Public Documents, an Apostille is sufficient. No consular authentication is required. * 11. CSCA Test Transcript(s) -You need to take the official CSCA test organized by the Chinese government and submit the corresponding subject result transcript(s) when applying. Learn more about the CSCA test >> -The test covers Chinese (Humanities and STEM Chinese), Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry. Mathematics is required for all programs, while other subjects depend on the university’s specific requirements. -We are updating detailed information for each university, including the required subjects you have to take for each program and their score requirements. Once the updates are ready, you can check the attachment and information here for this university for the latest information. If no attachment is available yet, it usually means the university has not announced further details. You can download a template or sample from here . Tips: For applicants who are in China: If you are an employee, you still need to provide employment separation certificate and your current residence permit. If you are a student, you need to provide transfer certificate, leaving certificate, certificate of attendance rate issued by previous school and your current residence permit.

The B.Sc. Computer Science is a sandwich program that allows students to gain valuable real world work experience. Graduates can easily leverage this strong foundation to specialize in various technical and managerial positions. Note: Time spent in foreign countries for more than 9 months in a year can be counted as one year.Entry and exit signatures will be used to verify residency. 1.3 Language Proficiency Requirements Applicants must meet the following language proficiency requirements based on the language of instruction for their chosen major: For International School (English-Taught Majors): Non-native English speakers must demonstrate English proficiency through one of the following: - IELTS: Minimum overall score of 5.5, with no section below 5.0 - TOEFL (IBT): Minimum score of 80 - SAT: Minimum total score of 1030

fields.description: Program Description Note: Degree students will study and live in the North Campus-Beijing Business School in Qijiazhen, Changping District, Beijing for first year. Then stuednts will move back to the main campus since the second year. Overview China Women’s University (CWU) is the first women’s higher learning Institution in modern China since 1949. It is affiliated with All-China Women’s Federation and academically administered by the Ministry of Education. It is a university specialized in women’s higher education and research in related areas. As the largest women institute of higher learning in China, and the only one, It offers graduate degree programs and under-graduate programs exclusively for women. CWU has now 7 schools and 4 departments. Other than the undergraduate and gradate programs, CWU also offers high vocational education, adults continuing education, and training programs for women leaders, etc. The current student number studying on campus is around 5,500 from all through China. Over 95% of them are female. Dedicated to Women’s higher education, CWU is established as a new force of forming more future women leaderships in China. Department of Teaching Chinese to Speakers of Other Languages The Department of teaching Chinese to sparkers of other language of CWU was established in 2009, which is the full member of the international society for Chinese language teaching, one of the main members in several Higher education cooperation systems. It offers female talents training programs for teaching Chinese as a foreign language, female college students practice innovation and entrepreneurship employment, and achieved abundant research results. More than 80% of graduates passed the Hanban headquarters’ International Chinese teachers selection, and have been sent abroad to work in the international Chinese education teaching. Graduate Programs CWU provides a joint graduate program with other universities offering master degrees in 5 disciplines of civil and commercial law, accounting, pre-school education, sociology and finance, and enrolls graduate students independently for Master of Social Works (MSW) and Master of Pre-school Education. Strong Subjects and Research Specialties CWU is specialized and at its strength in the disciplines of social work, preschool education, and women’s studies. In addition, the disciplines of finance, accounting, human resources, tourism management, international mandarin teaching, computer science and English are also among the most favorite subjects in CWU.

fields.description: Program Description 1. Program Overview Editor Notes: It offers students a most pertinent and unique combination of subjects, addressing contemporary Chinese business concerns, Chinese culture, Asian values and advanced Western and American business practice and management. International business introduces students to the world of global business. Courses cover the basics of the global economy, cultural influences on business, the impact of government decisions on business, what form of business to choose, importing and exporting goods and services, foreign exchange, and international management topics. 2. Core Courses Editor Notes: Courses may change every year, so the courses listed below are only for reference. International Business, Strategic Management, International Business Negotiation, Entrepreneurship, Mathematics for Business, Human Resource Management, Chinese Culture & Business Etiquette, International Trade. 3. Program Characteristics Editor Notes: You can known more about this program from the following characteristics. 1. An internationalized curriculum coupled with Chinese studies (Chinese language, culture, economics, business, laws and social studies) 2. An international faculty and internationally experienced Chinese professors who offer both the international and Chinese perspectives on contemporary business issues 3. Immersion Week: visits to Fortune 500 companies and top Chinese companies every semester 4. Internships and employment opportunities in multinational companies and organizations in China 5. Diversity in student composition: students from over 80 countries are empowered to develop cross-cultural communication skills in everyday life 6. Full integration with Chinese students, providing an opportunity to network with the top Chinese students 7. Home-Stay opportunities and Extended Family experience: Live with local Chinese families and immerse yourself in real Chinese community 8. Scholarship available for excellent students. 4. Introduction of International Business School Editor Notes: IBS is committed to be a first-class international business school to cultivate business elites with best foreign language and cross-cultural capabilities in China. The International Business School (IBS) is one of the youngest and most vigorous schools of Beijing Foreign Studies University (BFSU). In keeping with the international vision of BFSU, IBS has launched English-based programs for international students. Its mission is to offer students a highly enriching and rewarding multi-disciplinary learning experience with its excellent business-related courses and professional Chinese language teaching, thus helping ensure its students' success as future managers and executives in the global economy. Our graduates are well versed in the latest business management theory and practice. They are prepared to be responsible business leaders of the 21st Century with a specialized focus on the emerging and challenging business issues as China continues to become an important economic partner for many developed economies. Learn More>> 5. Campus Life Editor Notes: International students enjoy the wonderful life in the campus. International Students Performed in CCTV ​ BFSUers Preform at Asian Cultural Carnival ​​

fields.description: Program Description 1. Program Overview Editor Notes: This program develops the skills necessary to work in the fields of international marketing and international investment. This program is established on the fundamental economics and emphasizes on the theories and policies of international economics, international trade, and overseas investment in the global economy, as well as on the operation of international trade and overseas investment in real world practices . 2. Main Courses Editor Notes: Students will study 6 major courses. Macroeconomics, Microeconomics, International Finance, International Marketing, International Trade, History of Chinese Foreign Trade 3. Graduation​ Editor Notes: After completing this program, students can be equipped with solid foundation of field theory on international economics and trade, skills required for practices on international trade and investment, and skills of multicultural communication. Graduates are expected to acquire knowledge and capabilities as follows: The basic theories behind economics, commerce, finance, managementand accounting. Understand the economic and trade policies in major countries and districts as well as the current theories of international economics and trade. Have a deep understanding of current economic and social issues, which is guided by their broad international outlook to be capable of making economic analysis and decisions, international business negotiations, and practicing import and export operations. 4. Brief Introduction to Shanghai University Editor Notes: SHU is one of the top 40 Chinese universities, top 100 Asian universities, the premier university of Shanghai. Shanghai University is one of the key universities in the "Project 211". The current president of the university is Professor CHIEN Weichang, a famous educator, scientist, social activist and member of Chinese Academy of Sciences. The Party Secretary of Shanghai University is Professor YU Xinhui and the Executive Vice President is Professor ZHOU Zhewei. fields.description: Program Description Requirements for Chinese Level Generally students are required to pass HSK 6 before studying at BIPT except for the following: Chinese language students do not have to pass HSK. After the test for their Chinese level given by BIPT, they will start at the appropriate level. For some programs taught in English, students do not have to pass HSK. With application visiting students do not have to meet the requirements for Chinese level or pass HSK. Instead, they are required to have a good knowledge of English. Application for Chinese Government Scholarship The application will be submitted to the local agency or institution in charge of student dispatch or to the local Chinese embassy. The application period is from January to April every year. Duration of Study and Certificate An academic year is divided into three semesters: autumn semester( from early September to the next mid January),spring semester (from mid February to late June) and summer (from July to August).In summer semester students have field practice and short-term language training courses. The duration of study generally ranges from 1 semester to 2 academic years. Students will be issued a certificate for the course of study and will not be granted a degree, provided that they have passed all the issued a certificate for the course of study or will drop out of school. Chinese Teaching Long-term (form six months to one year) basic Chinese and pragmatic Chinese courses (including oral Chinese, listening, grammar and reading and writing) are given at BIPT in spring or autumn semester. Students will start at the appropriate level (primary, junior or senior).Besides, some elective courses are available, such as Chinese handwriting, ancient Chinese, appreciation of Chinese opera and movie, Chinese boxing, guidance in HSK, etc.

fields.description: Program Description 1. Program Description Editor Notes: The program focuses upon the Chinese legal system, laws and regulations and transacting international business in China. The program's objective is to provide foreign law professionals and students a foundation in Chinese law, while ensuring their adaption to a Chinese cultural and working environment. Designed to expose students to both the legal theory and legal practice, the program includes full-time study of the law in the first year and the option of writing a thesis or participating in an internship in the second year. LLM applicants are welcome to apply from different career backgrounds, including lawyers working in private law firms and government, government officials, law educators, businessmen and businesswomen and law school J.D. gradutates. The LLM program runs for a period of 2 years. The first year is for taking the classes and the second year is for completing the dissertation and taking internships. 2. Program Structure Editor Notes: The first year consists of two semesters and this year's available courses are listed below. 2.1 Compulsory & Optional Courses Compulsory Courses Optional Courses Introduction to Chinese Law Chinese Political and Legal System Chinese Contract Law Legal Writing Chinese Tort Law Chinese Company Law Chinese Constitutional and Administrative Law Legal Research Chinese Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure Basic Chinese Language Foreign Trade Laws and Regulations in China Introduction to Common Law System Foreign Investment, Merger and Acquisition in China Chinese Intellectual Property Law Chinese Civil Procedure & Arbitration Law Intellectual Property Law Chinese Banking Law and Capital Markets Chinese Insolvency Law and Corporate Reorganizations Chinese Labor Law and Social Security Investment Law 2.2 Trial Classes There are some free trial classes available online for prospective students to get a feel for the program. These introductory classes cover the following areas of Chinese law. Introduction to the Rule of Law in China Setting up or acquiring a business in China China Bankruptcy Law China & the WTO: Current Issues Dispute Resolution Processes in China China Anti-Monopoly Laws 3. Scholarships Scholarships are available for students who want to study on the Residential LLM Program. 4. Dissertation The dissertation should not be more than 12,000 words. Students are required to complete a defense of their dissertation in order to be awarded the LLM. 5. Internships Editor Notes: The School will make inquiries into suitable internships when students are enrolled on the program through connections with the law school. ​Students who are enrolled on the program will have the opportunity to take work experience at a top 5 law firm in China at any point during the two years they are enrolled on the LLM program. The internship period depends on each student and the type of internship that they seek. The purpose of the internship is to gain practical experience and skills working in a Chinese law firm. 6. School Introduction Editor Notes: It is a key university directly affiliated with the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China. Founded in 1941, Beijing Foreign Studies University (BFSU) is the first institution specializing in foreign language studies. It has the longest history among universities of its kind in China, offering a complete range of degrees, diplomas and programs at various levels, with the largest number of foreign language programs in the country. Excellence in teaching and extensive research in foreign language and literature has earned high respect for BFSU’s quality programs, both at home and internationally , Learn More>> 7. Law School of Beijing Foreign Studies University Editor Notes: LLM Program in China Business and Commercial Law is designed to expose students to the legal environment in China The faculty comes from varied backgrounds in the legal profession bringing expertise and experience. The professors are respected scholars, legal practitioners, jurists,legal theorists and researchers. The School has professors who have doctoral degrees and are nationally and internationally recognized al well as adjunct faculty, including leading Justices of the Supreme People's Court, senior judges and prosecutors, partners of leading international law firms, in-house counsel of state-owned enterprises and financial institutions and multinational companies in China. 8. Campus Life Editor Notes: International students enjoy the wonderful life in the campus. Moot Court Competition

fields.requirements: Entry Requirements 1. Non-Chinese citizens with a valid ordinary foreign passport, in good physical and mental health. 2. Sufficient financial resources; no criminal record. 3. Applicants who meet the following conditions are eligible to apply as international students: (1) Applicants who emigrated from mainland China, Hongkong, Taiwan or Macao, and have obtained a foreign nationality. (2) Applicants who acquired a foreign nationality at the time of birth, and whose parents (either or both) hold Chinese nationality (nationalities) and reside abroad. --- International applicants in the above situation must fulfill both two conditions following: ① Applicants must have held a valid foreign passport or nationality certificate for more than 4 years (inclusive), which means having acquired a foreign nationality before May 1, 2022. ② Applicants must have lived outside mainland China/Hong Kong/Macao/Taiwan for at least two years during the period from May 1, 2022 to April 30, 2026 (according to the entry and exit record, if the applicant has stayed outside mainland China/Hong Kong/Macao/Taiwan for nine months or longer period during one year, it is equivalent to one year). 4. Age Requirements: Self-funded applicants: be at least 16 years old and under the age of 35. 5. Educational Background: have obtained a graduation certificate of higher secondary school, or its international equivalent, qualified for university entrance. 6. Language Proficiency: For Chinese-taught programs: a minimum HSK Level 4 Certificate (score ≥180) & provide HSKK score. Important Note: To enroll in an undergraduate program at Donghua University, applicants must possess genuine Chinese proficiency equivalent to HSK Level 5 (with a minimum score of 180) or higher. Higher scores are strongly preferred. An HSK Level 4 score (above 180) or an HSK Level 5 score (below 180) can only be used for application purposes and is only valid during the application stage. If a conditional offer is received, a newly obtained HSK Level 5 certificate (with a score above 180) must be submitted to the university before the enrollment & registration. Failure to do so will result in the inability to register and commence undergraduate studies. ① The test date on the certificate must be on or after September 1, 2024. ② Applicants whose higher secondary school curriculum and teaching-related activities were conducted entirely in Chinese may be exempted from submitting an HSK certificate. requirements.text: Entry Requirements 1. Non-Chinese citizens with a valid ordinary foreign passport, in good physical and mental health. 2. Sufficient financial resources; no criminal record. 3. Applicants who meet the following conditions are eligible to apply as international students: (1) Applicants who emigrated from mainland China, Hongkong, Taiwan or Macao, and have obtained a foreign nationality. (2) Applicants who acquired a foreign nationality at the time of birth, and whose parents (either or both) hold Chinese nationality (nationalities) and reside abroad. --- International applicants in the above situation must fulfill both two conditions following: ① Applicants must have held a valid foreign passport or nationality certificate for more than 4 years (inclusive), which means having acquired a foreign nationality before May 1, 2022. ② Applicants must have lived outside mainland China/Hong Kong/Macao/Taiwan for at least two years during the period from May 1, 2022 to April 30, 2026 (according to the entry and exit record, if the applicant has stayed outside mainland China/Hong Kong/Macao/Taiwan for nine months or longer period during one year, it is equivalent to one year). 4. Age Requirements: Self-funded applicants: be at least 16 years old and under the age of 35. 5. Educational Background: have obtained a graduation certificate of higher secondary school, or its international equivalent, qualified for university entrance. 6. Language Proficiency: For Chinese-taught programs: a minimum HSK Level 4 Certificate (score ≥180) & provide HSKK score. Important Note: To enroll in an undergraduate program at Donghua University, applicants must possess genuine Chinese proficiency equivalent to HSK Level 5 (with a minimum score of 180) or higher. Higher scores are strongly preferred. An HSK Level 4 score (above 180) or an HSK Level 5 score (below 180) can only be used for application purposes and is only valid during the application stage.
